placet.title: Placet Group — Mobile Application
placet.description: Complete mobile app redesign with focus on clarity, control, and trust. Rebuilt user scenario architecture, financial states, and card journey.
placet.listDescription: Mobile app redesign focused on clear financial states and next best actions across loans, credit line, and card scenarios.
placet.challenge: Managing consumer finance is inherently stressful. Users seek clarity, predictability, and control, yet most financial apps overwhelm them with numbers, legal language, and fragmented flows. Placet's mobile experience suffered from inconsistent user journeys, unclear financial states, and non-uniform interface logic across loans, credit lines, and card features.
placet.solution: I redesigned the Placet app end-to-end with a focus on calm structure, transparency, and instant comprehension. Authentication was rebuilt using Smart-ID, Mobile-ID, and Face ID to establish trust from the first interaction. The dashboard follows a glance-first model, showing balance, next payment, and actions within seconds. A multi-state financial architecture was designed: processing, active, overdue, and empty states. The transaction feed was rebuilt into a dense but readable list with clear hierarchy and color-coded amounts. A full physical card journey was designed: ordered, shipped, expected delivery, activation, and active use. Both dark and light themes share a unified premium fintech visual language.
placet.result: Reduced support load, increased on-time payments, more predictable user experience.

screen1.title: Authentication & Face ID onboarding
screen1.description: The journey starts with a secure but minimal login flow using Smart-ID, Mobile-ID and Face ID. The goal is to remove friction while keeping the visual tone calm and trustworthy.

screen2.title: Dashboard — credit line at a glance
screen2.description: A high-level overview of the user's financial situation: remaining amount, next payment date and upcoming payment. The layout is optimised for quick scanning and daily use.

screen3.title: Financial states — processing, active and overdue
screen3.description: Different UI states explain what is happening with the credit line: application in processing, active credit with transactions, a clean empty state and an overdue state with a clear but non-aggressive warning.

screen4.title: Card ordering and delivery timeline
screen4.description: A step-based flow for physical card ordering: ordered, shipped and expected delivery. The UI uses a simple progress line and copy that reduces anxiety around where the card is in the journey.

screen5.title: Black Card controls and safety tools
screen5.description: Once the card is active, users get a control panel for contactless payments, internet transactions, temporary freeze and PIN tools. Each control is designed as a clear, tappable tile with strong hierarchy.

screen6.title: Visual system — dark & light explorations
screen6.description: Two visual directions: a deep, premium dark mode for fintech and a lighter, airy version for clarity. Both share the same structure and interaction patterns, making the system scalable.

paskolos.title: Paskolos.lt — Credit Line
paskolos.description: Credit line product design with emphasis on transparency of terms and informed decision-making.
paskolos.listDescription: Credit line product design focused on transparent terms, limit management, and confident user decision-making.
paskolos.challenge: At the entry point, users need to quickly understand the difference between a credit line and a consumer loan and choose the scenario that fits their needs. Without a clear structure and readable offers, the decision becomes unclear and trust in the conditions drops before the application even starts.
paskolos.solution:
I separated the two products through distinct hero screens while keeping a consistent offer language.
For the Consumer Loan, I combined key benefits and a 3-step application flow into a single block.
For the Credit Line, I highlighted the core mechanics through a limit selection calculator.
The journey was further supported with product recommendations and a final trust-building block.
paskolos.result: The site structure became clearer: Credit Line as the main entry point and Consumer Loan as a separate user scenario. Offers are readable from the first screen, CTAs are supported by explanatory blocks, and trust is reinforced before moving to application.

placetSelfservice.title: Placet Group — Unified Self-Service
placetSelfservice.description: Unified self-service platform for multiple brands: loans, cards, documents, support.
placetSelfservice.listDescription: Unified self-service platform enabling users to manage loans, cards, and documents in one account across multiple brands.
placetSelfservice.challenge: Previously, each Placet Group brand — smsraha, laen.ee, smsmoney and others — operated its own self-service environment. Users had different accounts, entry points and slightly different interfaces depending on the brand where they started. This fragmented experience caused confusion, increased support load and made it harder to understand the full customer relationship.
placetSelfservice.solution: I designed a unified self-service portal acting as a shared account layer across all Placet Group brands. Regardless of entry brand, users access a single environment with one login. The UX is built around a brand-agnostic core: a shared dashboard with all products, balances, payments and agreements, while preserving brand identity. Navigation and action flows were unified across all products.
placetSelfservice.result: Simplified product structure, increased trust, and reduced confusion between brands.
